meta.description: EN follow-up fixes: holy->honored mistranslations, badge errors, missing content. Verified against The Message. Source NOT modified.
meta.validation: all content/badge fix olds byte-identical to allBibleData.json (0 mismatches); no duplicate paragraph targets; every fix cites The Message; no blanket replacements

fixes.old: Why? Because you're a special crew, set apart for God, your God. He literally chose you out of everyone on Earth to be His personal treasure. That's some HONORED treatment right there.
fixes.new: Why? Because you're a special crew, set apart for God, your God. He literally chose you out of everyone on Earth to be His personal treasure. That's some HOLY treatment right there.
fixes.message_ref: MSG Deut 7:6: 'Do this because you are a people set apart as holy to God, your God. God, your God, chose you out of all the people on Earth for himself as a cherished, personal treasure.'
fixes.reason: The Message says 'holy', not honored. EN's caps-lock 'HONORED treatment' is exactly the holy→honored mistranslation. Restored 'HOLY' in the same teen-voice sentence.

Listen to my passionate prayers that I'm laying out before you right now. fixes.old: This is Paul, and I'm on a mission for Jesus Christ. He's the real MVP, and I'm part of his religious leaders, chosen to spread the word about God's awesome power. I'm writing this to all of you in Rome who are on God's team—you're the real honored ones.

fixes.message_ref: MSG Romans 1:6-7: "You are who you are through this gift and call of Jesus Christ!" / "God's love has poured out on you" — belonging/calling, not an 'honored' rank.

God trusted them to write down his words, the Holy Scriptures. But what if some of them bailed on their mission? Does that mean God ghosted them? No way! God always keeps his promises, even when everyone else is being fake. Like the Scriptures say, "Your words are always true, even when people reject you."

fixes.old: Let me break it down even more. Our old, cringey self was basically crucified with Christ. That whole miserable life where sin was calling the shots? It's over. Canceled. We're not stuck with its demands anymore. Here's the core belief: if we were part of Christ's death that totally owned sin, we're also part of his resurrection that gives us life. We know that when Jesus came back from the dead, it was the ultimate mic drop on death itself. Death doesn't get the final say anymore. When Jesus died, he took sin down with him. But now that he's alive, he connects us directly to God. So from now on, think of it like this: sin is a dead language, it's totally irrelevant to you. But God? He's speaking your language, and you should be hanging on every word. You're done with sin and totally alive for God. That's the honored treatment Jesus gives you.

fixes.old: So, let's get the lineup straight. God is the head honcho, Jesus reports to God, and in a family, the husband is the team lead for the wife. It's all about respecting the chain of command. If a guy is praying or talking about God but acting like he's the boss instead of Jesus, he's totally disrespecting the real honored. Same goes for a wife who publicly disses her husband's role—it makes them both look bad. It's just an terrible look, like a girl who has to shave her head. That's basically why we have these customs: guys take their hats off to show respect to Jesus, and women wear a covering to show they're part of the team structure. It's a visual way of saying, 'We're not fighting for control; we're all under God's ultimate authority.'

fixes.old: You can tell Melchizedek was a total honored because even Father Abraham, the guy who started it all, gave him a ten percent cut of his winnings. Think about it: the priests from Levi's tribe, who are all related to Abraham, have a rule to collect a tenth from their own people.
